parcalar.metin: On the night of August twenty-first, nineteen eighty-six,
a lake in the hills of Cameroon exhaled.

cumleler.altyazi: On the night of 21 August 1986, a lake in the hills of Cameroon exhaled.

parcalar.metin: There was no fire. No flood. No explosion.
Just a silent cloud of carbon dioxide,
rising from the bottom of Lake Nyos.
parcalar.soyle: rising from the bottom of Lake Nee-ohss.

parcalar.metin: The gas was heavier than air.
By morning, one thousand seven hundred and forty-six people were dead,
and three thousand five hundred animals.

cumleler.altyazi: By morning, 1,746 people were dead, and 3,500 animals.

parcalar.metin: Volcanic gas had been slowly building up deep in the water,
parcalar.soyle: Volcanic gas had been slowly building up, deep in the water,

parcalar.metin: until the lake could not hold it.
Today, pipes vent that gas safely,
shooting fountains high above the lake.
nearby Lake Monoun had done the same.
parcalar.soyle: nearby Lake Mon-oon had done the same.

parcalar.metin: Would you live beside a lake that can breathe?
And which deadly place on Earth should we explore next?
